nodes.description: The initiating lesions are homozygous MAP3K20 variants affecting the C-terminal SAM domain: the missense variant c.1103T>G p.(Phe368Cys) in the Pakistani family and a 14.7-kb intragenic deletion of exons 12-16 in the Tunisian family. The SAM domain is present only in the long ZAK-alpha isoform; the short ZAK-beta isoform lacks it, so both lesions alter ZAK-alpha specifically.

nodes.description: ZAK-alpha is normally activated when its SAM domains dimerize on collided ribosomes. The SFMMP missense variant p.Phe368Cys is already fully autophosphorylated without induced ribosome collisions and can bypass the ribosome requirement. Whether this hyperactivity occurs in developing limb cells, or applies to the SAM-deletion allele, has not been tested.

evidence.reference_title: ZAK activation at the collided ribosome.
evidence.snippet: As expected, ANS treatment induced autophosphorylation of WT ZAK but did not change the extent of phosphorylation of F368C and K387D, which were already fully activated before ANS treatment

evidence.reference_title: ZAK activation at the collided ribosome.
evidence.snippet: Characterization of novel SAM variants as well as a known pathogenic variant of the SAM domain of ZAK supports a key role of the SAM domain in regulating kinase activity on and off the ribosome, with some mutants bypassing the ribosome requirement for ZAK activation.

nodes.description: Abnormal patterning of the central rays of the developing foot, producing the cleft, the partial second-ray duplication, syndactyly and phalangeal hypoplasia and fusion seen on radiographs. Zak is expressed in the developing mouse limbs, and SAM-deleted mice develop variable hindlimb duplication and polydactyly with low penetrance (4 of 64 animals). The hands are spared apart from the nails.

nodes.description: p.Phe368Cys sits in the hydrophobic core of the SAM domain. The purified mutant domain loses about a third of its alpha-helicity, loses cooperative thermal unfolding and is aggregation prone. The exon 12-16 deletion is predicted to remove the SAM domain entirely. These measurements were made on isolated domains, not on full-length protein in limb cells.
